Record Class CausalViolation

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.parsley.CausalViolation
Record Components:
record - the offending record, as the original Kafka ConsumerRecord; never null
reason - why the record violated causal order; never null
frontier - the frontier at the moment of the violation; never null
required - the dependencies the record required to be delivered in order; never null (empty if the record carried no resolvable dependencies)
gap - the per-position shortfall (required − observed) for every position the frontier had not caught up on; the CausalPosition.offset() field of each entry holds the shortfall amount, not an absolute log offset; empty if required.isSatisfiedBy(frontier)
public record CausalViolation(org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecord<?,?> record, CausalViolationReason reason, CausalFrontier frontier, CausalDependencies required, List<CausalPosition> gap) extends Record
A causal-ordering violation, reported to a CausalViolationHandler with enough context to act on or audit it.

A violation arises when a record cannot be delivered in strict causal order — it carried unresolvable dependencies, no dependencies attribute, or was evicted from the buffer because a CausalBufferLimit fired. The payload carries the causal gap: what the frontier had observed (frontier) versus what the record required (required), and the per-position shortfall (gap) — the difference between a violation you can operate around (replay, compensate, alert) and one you can only find in a postmortem.

      • Constant Field Values

    • DLQ_REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES_HEADER

      public static final String DLQ_REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES_HEADER
      Name of the header stamped on every dead-lettered record: the required CausalDependencies, encoded via CausalDependencies.toBytes() and decodable via CausalDependencies.fromBytes(byte[]).

      Replay path

      1. Decode the required dependencies: CausalDependencies.fromBytes(header.value()).
      2. Wait until your consumer's frontier satisfies them (i.e. it has observed every position the original record required).
      3. Re-produce the original record with the same parsley-causal-dependencies value, stripping the parsley-dlq-* headers first.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • DLQ_GAP_HEADER

      public static final String DLQ_GAP_HEADER
      Name of the header stamped on every dead-lettered record: the per-position causal shortfall at eviction time, encoded as a CausalDependencies value via CausalDependencies.toBytes(). Each entry's CausalPosition.offset() is the shortfall (required − observed). Useful for diagnostics; not needed for replay.
